item.title: The Recursive Dollhouse
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fridge Horror/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: Essentially, SCP-XXXX a dollhouse of whatever environment it is currently being contained within. Likewise, it would sustain a diminished capability of whatever building it is housed in. SCP-XXXX-1 are essentially "dolls" housed in the facility that make up sentient/concious organisms. This also applies to anomalous materials as well, such as me, the toaster that speaks in the first person or the mask SCP. In addition, the anomalous effects of objects are still maintained but to a much smaller degree. Objects within the SCP-XXXX move in tandem with their current reality counterparts. Actions made within the main facility are mirrored in SCP-XXXX. There is in fact a miniature version of SCP-XXXX (dubbed SCP-XXXXa) and it is theorized that there are multiple versions of SCP-XXXX that exist within the dimensional realm.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation found this dollhouse in the middle of a nursery amongst other toys. After examining this, an entity attempts to contact them (potentially, though I am not sold on the concept) in an attempt to get it back.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The inherent dread of a recursive universe where what we view from within could in fact be caused by an upper plane of existence is terrifying, no?

Additional Notes: Edit 1: As for what happens when objects or instances of SCP-XXXX-1 are affected by outside users, I'd like to go into that further within test logs potentially. If not, essentially, the-what I dub-"dollhouse reality" can be affected by users. The current reality would be marginally affected in a similar manner. This isn't compulsory, however, but it does bring about satisfaction of the affected individual to complete said task. Other more violent actions such as the destruction of an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 can cause a severely minimized effect on the affected individual.If an anomalous SCP-XXXX-1 instance comes in contact with a non-anomalous instance of SCP-XXXX-1, the effects that would be generated by the anomalous instance are greatly minimized. Objects brought into the SCP-XXXX reality will manifest in the current reality as well.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) 'In Your Dreams: An instructional video on how to get the best sleep possible'
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological Horror

Page Layout (Optional): More or less a traditional SCP article, though I plan to include a transcript of the tape and test results of those who viewed the tape.

Elevator Pitch: This SCP takes the form of a video tape. It is labelled 'In Your Dreams: an instructional video on how to get the best sleep possible' It starts out as a sleep instructional video before descending into madness, including subliminal messaging. The contents of the tape lead to massive psychological effects on whoever views the whole thing.

Central Narrative: The tape was discovered in the home of a suicide victim. The individual had no psychological issues prior to the viewing of the tape, which caught the attention of the SCP foundation. Attempts to find any info on the tape's origin has proven unsuccessful. However, the foundation has discovered multiple cases of homicides and suicides linked to this tape. All of the people who have viewed the tape and comply with all of its instructions suffer from insomnia, delusions, prone to self harm, sociopathic tendencies, and decreased empathy/compassion. Some extreme cases include incoherent rambling, and repeating the phrase "THERE ARE NO FACES."

In one incident, a copy of the tape was reportedly aired on TV in Mason County, Washington. Those who viewed the tape have received Class A amnesiacs, which have been proven successful with reversing the tapes effects

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There will be a disclaimer on the top stating that any staff who view the tape will be subject to Class A amnesiacs and an emergency psychological evaluation and that any unauthorized viewing of the tape will lead to termination, and any attempts at distributing the tape will lead to termination or reassignment to D-class.

Additional Notes: This was inspired by Local58's "real sleep". Honestly, the whole series is SCP material.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Muse
item.description: A being that pretends to be a person's subconscious.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Psychological Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard + Exploration logs

Elevator Pitch: From the perspective of the affected, a voice calls to them from inside their head, claiming to be their subconscious. It helps them along, allows them to remember things better, formulate ideas faster, etc. After a while, it will take the form of a humanoid hallucination, engaging in long conversations with the victim. The victim becomes more and more detached from reality, spiraling into ritual and insanity as the "muse" takes over more and more of their mind, eventually taking full control of their body.

Central Narrative: A small foundation site collapses as the head researcher comes under the affect of the Muse.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reveal of the muse not being a figment of the victim's mind but rather an independent entity.

Additional Notes: I think this could either turn out very good and interesting or very cliché.

item.title: Parasitic Amoeba
item.description: An Amoeba that is really fast and attacks the heart.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX Is a species of omnivorous amoeba that travel extremely fast throughout liquids and can terminate any organism in seconds.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX-1 usually appears to those who have a small paycheck and have ease of access to a large container for water. Then SCP-XXXX-1 will dump a colony of SCP-XXXX into said container when the owner is near it. After dumping the colony the owner of the container will be frozen in place while SCP-XXXX walks towards and eventually into them, tell them to take care of the colony and then de-manifest.

Attention Grabber: I feel like there are a lot of SCPs that are either monstrous, cute or funny. But not all SCPs have to be that way. Another thing is that one thing goes through my head every time I hear of a K-Class end of the world scenario, that the world can be ended by something as big as a meteor or something as small as a micro-organism. I feel like there aren't enough small organisms in foundation custody that are capable of causing such an event.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Abnormal High School
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Genre: Action

Elevator Pitch: twenty-five (25) humanoids, thirteen (13) male humanoids, and twelve (12) female humanoids that're infected by an unknown phenomenon in an abandoned high school that turns them into mutants with dangerous abilities.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX, also known as "The Abnormal High School," is a high-school located somewhere deep in the woods, abandoned due to the place where it was being built was used as a testing zone for nuclear weapons of the government. In the year 2006, twenty-five individuals who are runaways had entered the school as they experienced a mysterious headache that causes them to faint for a long time after they were awake; they've discovered that they're not normal anymore, or to be specific; they have become something that cannot be explained. SCP-XXXX was brought to the Foundation's attention when they've received witness reports of a boy levitating in the middle of the air, at the same time altering the wind, as they've discovered that the humanoid male is located in an area with nuclear waste. This resulted in dispatching as Task-Force MTF Beta-7 as they were a success in retrieving all of the subjects that're in SCP-XXXX

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The origins of SCP-XXXX trace back to the early 19s. A mysterious asteroid landed into the abandoned high-school after it was tested by the government's nuclear weapons, which the school was completely obliterated into oblivion. However, with the asteroid's presence, it has been reconstructed back as new.

item.content:encoded:

Elevator pitch: The SCP is a dog that can summon and redirect lighting. Most of the time it looks and acts like a normal dog except a tear in it's flesh on it's left shoulder blade.

Central narrative: SCP-XXXX draws electricity into it's body so no open electrical devices can be near it. When electricity enters it's body, it turns hostile and attacks anything near it. It stays like this for around 10-30 minutes depending on the amount of electricity that entered it's body.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It was found near a power plant in England after the police reported a dog "throwing lightning at them".

item.title: A helping hand (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP involves a floating hand which assists people with things when they are needed, the SCP teleports to anyone who says they need help with something, this will not work if they are only thinking of needing help and not saying it,

Central Narrative: The hand is cut off at the wrist area, the inside shows a black void.
Testing showed that it can only help with things if it's within a 5 meter radius and will help with anything it can, it can hammer a nail in the wall, or shoot a target as long as it's within 5 meters of the person needing help.

It is able to teleport anywhere on the world and wont stay any longer than needed so containment isn't possible and has since been classified as Keter, it's presence was noticed by the foundation in 2011 when a twitter user Robert Hexain posted a message about the SCP who helped him repair his roof.

When there are multiple people in need of assistance it will randomly choose one to help and will help the other later if they still need help, during testing a tracker was put on the SCP to locate it at all times to see who the SCP helped, they will then be tracked down, interviewed and given Class B amnestics

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It can be helpful or it can be really dangerous

Additional Notes:

item.title: A video game that kills REVISION (seeking greenlight)
item.description: A video game that kills anyone who played it...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • The SCP is a video game cartridge with scratched up stickers and a scratched logo and title which is impossible to make out.
  • a video game cartridge that can be played on Nintendo 64, but no one1 remembers or knows about the game or the development of the game.
  • whenever a player dies in the video game, within 24 hours the player in real life would face the same fate as the player who died in the video game.

Central Narrative:
The SCP itself has no unusual properties and can be handled with ease, just simply, anyone can touch it, bite it, whatever. The SCP starts to act strange when the SCP is plugged into a Nintendo 64 console.

The SCP is a game cartridge with scratched-up stickers, there is no title but does have a brand name called "PlugSoft"2.

Important information about the thing: When the cartridge is plugged into a regular Nintendo 64, the player will be introduced into an open-world. When the player starts, the subject will appear to be in a trance focusing on the game ignoring anything like pain and loud noises, if the SCP is plugged out or the subject is removed from the screen the subject will immediately be in a hostile state killing anyone who interfered, and after killing, the subject will kill (him/her)self. The place that sets the player is a city called: "Alterio City", the player inside the game can virtually do ANYTHING3. Whenever the player dies, the subject will instantly die as the same fate.4

The SCP item was created by a 19-year-old male Korean programmer, possibly a PlugSoft developer, and wanted to make a game that gave people a city with no rules. The programmer was found dead5 with a note on his left hand. The note read about the programmer fighting depression and stress, and couldn't take anymore.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is special about this SCP is because I think (I THINK! I am not certain) that this SCP is the first video game that kills anyone. (Again, I am not certain, there is probably an SCP like this. I don't know…)

Additional Notes: I would LOVE! to see some criticism or feedback. Thank you!

Footnotes
1. as in people in a video game developing companies, as well as Nintendo
2. The PlugSoft is a video game company that produces anomalous 'video games.'
3. in that, they can commit any crime easily
4. if a player died of a car crash, the subject in the real world will die with the same injuries in the game
5. suicide, a gun was found on his right hand

item.title: SCP Idea: Stuck in the Past
item.description: 3 anomalous dial-up access numbers that take your computer back in time...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Basically, it's a set of three anomalous access dial-up Internet access numbers, each with the same anomalous property: when you connect to it, your web browser is pretty much transported back to the late 2000s. Everything is as it was back then: web sites, web services, social media are all unchanged from their original forms back then, and it can all be interacted with by users of this SCP. For all intents and purposes, this SCP is a technological time machine. Oh, and it's way faster than regulr dial-up.

Central Narrative: The Foundation discovers the existence of this SCP in 2017, and a few years later they use it to interview some people from the past. Through these interviews, they discover the possible origin of the SCP, and eventually they find one of its' creators. He sorta explains how it was made and why it was made, going in depth about the state of the modern internet and how much he hates it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There are many internet-based SCPs, but I have yet to see one which is directly affiliated with the internet itself rather than just using it as a medium through which to do its "thing". The internet is a big and scary place, and I feel like its many different subcultures and groups (and its history) have so much potential as a source of inspiration for SCPs. After all, without the internet, the Foundation wouldn't exist ;)

Additional Notes: I've already typed up a draft of the entire article + the chat/interview logs, if you want me to post it here I can.

Thanks for reading my idea, everyone! This is my second real SCP idea that I've posted here, and it's the first one that I'm really, truly super proud of ^u^ It's been such a long time, I honestly forgot how much I love writing…

item.title: Grant Request For Anti-Fire fire
item.content:encoded:
Page Type : SCP article and/or Prometheus Labs research paper

Elevator Pitch : The anomaly is a bunch of matchsticks that create an odd-colored fire. When that fire is put on regular fire, the regular fire will be burnt off by the normal fire. The explanation will be that the anomalous fire uses normal fire as fuel and burns off any approaching oxygen, thus taking down both fires

Central Narrative : Right after the description, a heavily shortened Prometheus Labs document will be there, revealing that it was found in a closed laboratory belonging to them.

The article will explain that due to the effort it takes to take down large fires, a scientist decided that the best solution will be to create anomalous fire which can burn fire. It was originally planned to be sold to civilians in the form of matches so that they can bring it around in case of fires (Due to the slow-acting nature of this, firefighters will probably stick to water). At first, the problem section is still being written.

Hook : An audio file which is discovered in another lab will be transcribed below, recording the voice of the scientist and his boss testing out prototypes. Several problems are quickly discovered by the boss. 1. For automatic fire extinguishing, sprinklers still outclass it. 2. The anomalous fire consumes oxygen, thus meaning that it can still cause smoke and suffocation, the most dangerous parts of a fire. 3. It does nothing to stop the spread of the normal fire if it's in a big enough space, thus only reducing the size of the fire. In the end, it is revealed that due to the problems discovered, the project is canceled.

Additional Notes : I wanted to try and write a tale of the creation of an anomalous object that in paper sounds useful yet in practice, it is noticeably terrible and why testing is extremely important.

item.title: Right Brained Sewing Machine.
item.description: A seemingly sapient sewing machine capable of producing clothing out of any material. Dark matter lingerie anyone?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A seemingly sapient sewing machine that is able to produce thread out of any material inserted into it. Rudimentary brain made out of millions of wires by its needle. Three knobs. One that controls the temperature inside the storage container, one that changes the settings of the machine depending on the material's hardness and another that changed how the machine sews. Third knob has 'Manual' option to manually use the machine, 'Automatic' option to create the desired outcome (input through speaking to machine) like a 3D printer and a 'Learning' option which makes the machine experiment with its own design and material used, creating some funky and inventive clothing items. Items created by the machine are not anomalous unless the material was anomalous. Can mix many types of material together. Can quickly respond to yes/no questions by using a high/low pitched beep. Responds to open-ended questions by sewing the answer together. Foundation uses this to 'interview' machine.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Incomplete origin, being investigated by Foundation. Discovered inside a Mumbai hotel room. Owners seized machine after the occupant, wealthy English woman Ollie Mae Price, went missing for more than 14 days. Owners were intrigued but could not figure out how to use the machine. Experimented with it and created a bra made of wool whilst using the automatic setting. Owners then made bras out of glass and porcelain. Began to sell the pieces on a street stall, stirring widespread rumours that ultimately reached The Foundation. Foundation questioned the owners briefly, dispensing Class B amnestics after seizing the machine. Foundation found some people from Dharavi wearing purple-dyed metallic shirts, coats and skirts. Suspicions arose that Ollie had been supplying clothes made by the machine to the Dharavian citizens for an unknown, possibly benevolent reason. Foundation now has an immense interest in the machine to efficiently create armours as well as replace lose laundry. Foundation interviews the machine to explore its origin, creator as well as the whereabouts of Ollie and what her motives were with the machine. Through continuous use of the 'learning' feature, the machine now knows how to make more complex items such as basic microchips and explosive devices. Machine uses the initals D.W when asked about who or what created them, nothing more.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The endless possibilities and uses The Foundation has with the machine, much like SCP-294. The machine's 'learning' feature establishes its own growth as an entity and how it is gaining knowledge and changing before The Foundation's eyes.

Additional Notes: If it's not Greenlight worthy yet, please send me some suggestions below! They will be very much appreciated.

item.title: The 14th
item.description: The twisted and queer mystery behind O5-14, and who he is.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Elevator Pitch: Currently, there are 13 members of the O5 council. However, there are speculations of a possible 14th member, who's been exiled from the SCP foundation. No one knows who he is, where he came from, and what happened to him.

Central Narrative: He exists, that's for sure. Most staff know him by now, the 14th member, or O5-14. He doesn't have a specified name, age, or appearance, we just know he exists. When spoken about in front of the O5 council, they're all usually quiet, and refuse to give details. One person who seems to be connected to the 14th member is a janitor, Raphael Moore. He's dead though, maybe. No information about him, he was only a janitor who knew one of O5's biggest secrets.

What happened to the 14th member? Quite simply, he was exiled. No one knows why he was exiled. A document confirming his exile was found in a cabinet, dating back to December 16th, 1855. Most of the document was either torn off, or burnt, only the date remained.

There are 3 sections to this tale. the 14th, the meeting, and the disappearance. In the first section, it explains who he was, and when he was exiled (of course, no one knows why). In the 2nd section, it takes place in 2019, a meeting held between the O5 council, and site directors of over 100 facilities, all wondering the same thing, "Who is the 14th?". Stalemate, obviously. Final section, the disappearance… of Raphael Moore, the man connected to the 14th. The disappearance of this man lead to HUGE speculation, investigations, and concerns within the SCP foundation, causing revolts, rebellions, all the fun ingredients for disaster.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Sure, a small tale, but a rather intriguing and mysterious tale.

Additional Notes: It probably sucks.

item.title: SCP idea: Retroactive weight gain supplement
item.description: A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but
item.content:encoded:
A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but it actually rewrites your memories to make you only think you have lost weight. Use it too much and your memories start getting weird.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Edit: Added the required template.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Page starts with basic containment procedures and a description. The main part of the narrative will be in the experiment log, which will reveal more about the effects of the SCP and may include interview logs with the test subjects.

Elevator Pitch: A scam supplement that is advertised as causing weight loss but it actually rewrites your memories to make you only think you have lost weight. Use it too much and your memories start getting weird.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP is a weight loss pill that you can order a subscription to though an anomalous phone number. Each pill rewrites your memories a little bit to make you believe you lost weight after taking the pill. Since it does not actually cause weight loss in the present, you probably will actually gain weight without knowing it. The more pills that are taken the fatter you will believe you used to be and the further back in time it changes your memories. Eventually, you will be convinced that you have been morbidly obese your entire life before you started taking the pills. If you keep taking the pills past this point (I will call this the critical point for now), things start to get strange. The boxes that the pills come in have two languages on them. One is English (or whatever language you speak) and is all lies, and the other is an unknown language. After the critical point, you gain the ability to read the unknown language, which tells the truth about what the pills do, and you start to gain memories from before you were born of being something not human.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It is a weight loss pill that retroactively turns users into gluttony monsters in human form, or at least makes them think they are.

Additional Notes: I haven't decided yet how much it affects other people's memories or physical records like pictures. I haven't decided yet what happens if you stop taking the pills, though it probably depends on if you have passed the critical point or not. I may end up leaving it ambiguous if it is actually changing the past or just your memories.

item.title: Safe class SCP: The Wrong Chair
item.description: a chair that is impossible to remain seated in
item.content:encoded:
The wrong chair is a chair that is impossible to remain seated in due to discomfort. If one remains seated anyway nearly harmless anomalous effects may occur.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Other (Simply a strange object)

Page Layout (Optional): Standard Format

Elevator Pitch: This is a chair, bench, or other form of seating that makes anyone that tries to sit there very uncomfortable with the idea of sitting there without any physical effects. It is not possible to contain, however, as it relocates via unknown means.

Central Narrative: The Wrong Chair almost always replaces damaged seating in seemingly random locations around the planet. It also has no uniformed appearance. Occasionally it will appear as an additional seat in a room instead of replacing a broken one. The Wrong Chair causes minor psychological distress to those seated on it until they move, but there is no lasting effects upon standing. If anyone manages to remain seated for more than 2 minutes and 37 seconds The Wrong Chair will disappear, leaving them to fall to the ground, or to land on top of the damaged seating The Wrong Chair formerly replaced. The Wrong Chair will always relocate within 24 hours, and always appears somewhere unobserved. In at least two cases it appeared when someone blinked, replacing a broken seat in the room they were in. ETC.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Simply enough this is just something bizarre but mostly harmless, yet impossible to contain.

Additional Notes: First try by me! People told me to submit the idea here from other locations.
